# The `project.nobara.lock` file

This page is the reference for `project.nobara.lock`, the file at the root of
a game that records every module of the game with the version it resolved
to, so that builds are reproducible. [`nobara generate`](../cli.md#nobara-generate)
writes it; it is kept in version control and never edited by hand.

## Example

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!-- Generated by nobara generate: the modules of the game and their resolved versions. Do not edit. -->
<NobaraLock format="1">
  <Module id="example.lighting" version="1.0.4" source="package" transitive="true" />
  <Module id="example.mobs" version="0.1.0" source="local" path="src/Example.Mobs" />
  <Module id="example.voxel" version="1.2.3" source="package" />
  <Module id="example.zombie" version="0.1.0" source="local" path="src/Example.Zombie" />
</NobaraLock>
```

## Root element

`<NobaraLock>` is the root element. Its `format` attribute holds the version
of the file format; the current format is `1`. It holds one `<Module>`
element per module of the game, sorted by identifier.

## `<Module>`

| Attribute | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | Identifier of the module. |
| `version` | Version of the module: of its `module.nobara` for a project, the version that NuGet restored for a package. |
| `source` | `local` for a `<Local>` entry of [`project.nobara`](project-nobara.md), `override` for a project that replaces a package, `package` for a NuGet package. |
| `path` | For `local` and `override`: the folder of the project, relative to the game, with forward slashes. |
| `transitive` | `true` when no entry of `<Modules>` names the module: another module requires it. Absent otherwise. |

## How the versions are used

Only the versions of packages are read back. When `nobara generate` resolves a
package again, it keeps the version of the lock file while that version
satisfies every range that requires the package; otherwise NuGet chooses the
lowest version that does, and the file records it. A build installs the
version of the lock file.

## Known limitations

- The file records no hash of the packages.
